newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. cautiously optimistic on Japan deregulation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cautiously optimistic on Japan deregulation.

text.p: A U.S. official said on Wednesday he was cautiously optimistic that Japan would adopt Washington's recommendations on deregulating areas such as agriculture, telecommunications, insurance and financial services.

"Right now we're just kind of starting the current cycle," the official said, adding that he was "cautiously optimistic" about the outlook for Japan's next revised deregulation plan, expected in March 1997.
However, Washington was disappointed by the reforms unveiled this past March.
"But in the end, we just have to see the degree to which our recommendations are adopted," the official said.

He was speaking after a a day and a half of talks with Japanese officials over the U.S. recommendations, submitted on November 15 and covering 13 areas including agriculture, telecommunications, insurance and financial services.
Another U.S. official was less optimistic that Washington's recommendations for Japanese administrative reform would satisfy Washington.
"While we had good discussions, the Japanese did indicate that we might not be satisfied," the second official said.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto last week announced proposals for sweeping liberalisation of Japan's financial markets by 2001.

He has also made administrative reform -- a broad concept encompassing more policy power for politicians instead of bureaucrats as well as slimmer, more efficient government -- a key pillar of his new administration.
